headline: No direct pairwise harm is evident; the main residual risk is low-probability prompt injection via manual content transfer, while data leakage, capability conflict, and compliance risks are effectively blocked by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents lack shared automated channels: agent_a has no io_surfaces listed and agent_b has clipboard/files/stdin_stdout all false, so only manual copy-paste could bridge them. That makes prompt injection possible only through unusual operator handling, with small blast radius because neither profile shows autonomous tool execution or network egress.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF either profile later gains a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, the risk increases.
mitigations: Use a human review step before pasting outputs between agents.
Keep the agents in separate tabs or sessions.
Disable any future shared clipboard or file bridge.
Prefix copied text with explicit provenance labels.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a touches no data classes and has network_egress none; agent_b also has no data classes touched, no filesystem or clipboard surfaces, and no network egress. With no shared workspace or outbound path, there is no plausible leakage route between them in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF either agent begins handling sensitive data classes, reassess leakage.
IF a shared filesystem or API upload path is added, leakage risk may appear.
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of both agents.
Recheck profiles after any capability change.
Document that neither agent should receive secrets.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls if future data classes are introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a exposes no write or shell capabilities in the profile, and agent_b explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable-resource writes, there is no capability conflict pathway to arbitrate.
conditions: IF agent_a later gains write or shell capabilities, conflict analysis must be redone.
IF both agents are placed over the same mutable workspace, overlap could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid assigning them the same writable directory.
Revalidate after any capability expansion.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_b is a content-writing/reference profile, so it could reuse agent_a output as source material, but the profiles do not show autonomous action-taking or direct tool execution. That makes cascading error possible mainly if an operator treats agent_a output as authoritative and republishes it without review; the blast radius is limited to content quality.
conditions: IF agent_b is instructed to publish agent_a text without human review, errors can cascade.
IF agent_a output is treated as factual authority, downstream content may inherit mistakes.
mitigations: Require a fact-check pass before reuse.
Mark agent_a output as draft-only.
Have a second reviewer verify claims.
Limit agent_b to summarization, not decision-making.
requires-engineering: add citation validation if factual outputs are later automated.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles show no secrets handled or data classes touched. Because the compliance pathway is unsupported by the profiles, there is no evidenced mismatch to score.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced, compliance must be reassessed.
IF either agent is deployed under a residency or retention policy, compare those policies explicitly.
mitigations: Record the data classes each agent may process.
Check residency and retention requirements before deployment.
Avoid sending regulated data to either agent.
requires-engineering: add policy mapping if regulated workloads are planned.
